name: Chin fat removal

card.summary: Procedures that reduce fat under the chin (submental fat), such as liposuction or deoxycholic acid injections, to sharpen the jawline and neck angle.
card.aka: double chin treatment, submental fat reduction
card.note: Fat removal does not tighten loose skin, and a double chin can also come from jaw structure rather than fat.

quick.overview:
Chin fat removal covers treatments that reduce the fat pad under the chin, often called a double chin, so the line between jaw and neck looks sharper. Options include surgical fat removal (liposuction or direct excision of fat and muscle tightening) and in-office injections of synthetic deoxycholic acid.

A double chin can come from excess fat, but also from a recessed jaw or chin that makes the chin appear to melt into the neck. Clinicians distinguish the two because fat removal addresses only the first.
quick.how: A doctor assesses whether the fullness is fat, skin laxity or bone structure. For fat, treatments range from a roughly 15-minute injection visit, usually repeated two to four times, to a surgical procedure with anaesthesia and a longer recovery. Loose skin may need a surgical lift instead.
quick.risks: Injections can cause temporary swelling, burning, bruising and numbness, which clinics say settle over days to weeks. Surgery carries the usual operative risks and a small scar. Treatments are cosmetic and generally not covered by insurance.

lead: Chin fat removal refers to reducing the subcutaneous fat beneath the chin to improve the contour between the jawline and neck. A double chin is defined as loss of definition of the jawbone or soft tissue under the chin, and it can result from excess fat or from a bony deficiency in which the jaw does not project far enough forward [1].

For fat-related double chins, surgical treatment can involve removing the fat pad and shortening muscle (a hyoid lift); for bony causes genioplasty or jaw surgery may be used [1]. Non-surgical injection of synthetic deoxycholic acid, sold as Kybella, breaks down fat cells under the chin during a short in-office visit, with most people needing two to four sessions [2].

In looksmaxxing, a sharper submental area is part of the goal of a defined jaw and neck. Surgical removal is the more invasive end of the options, and registered trials have explored techniques that use the submental fat itself, for example as a flap for chin enhancement [3].

chain: Clearer line from jaw to neck
angle.text: Removing submental fat reveals the jaw and neck contour that fullness had hidden. Where the issue is skin laxity or jaw structure, clinicians describe other procedures.

infobox: Fat pad removal, hyoid lift, genioplasty for bony causes

paras: In some overweight people subcutaneous fat around the neck forms a wrinkle that looks like a second chin. In people of normal weight a double chin is more often due to a jaw that does not project forward enough, so the chin appears to blend into the neck even with little fat present [1].

Surgical treatments for the fat-related form include fat pad removal and muscle shortening, described as often a purely cosmetic procedure; genioplasty or orthognathic surgery address bony deficiency, and early maxillomandibular advancement is described as the usual causal treatment when sleep apnoea is present [1].

A hospital health page describes Kybella as an in-office injection into the fat under the chin, a roughly 15-minute visit; the fat cells break down and the body clears them over a few weeks. It lists temporary swelling, burning, small bruises and numbness as side effects, notes it does not tighten loose skin, and says it suits moderate to severe pinchable fat [2]. The same page quotes a price of $1,200 per treatment at that centre and mentions CoolSculpting and liposuction as alternatives [2].

Registered trials include a completed 2015 study of 10 participants testing a fatty flap taken from the double chin for chin enhancement in people with adiposity and a small chin [3], and a 2024 study of 12 participants evaluating a deep-plane intervention in the submental region for managing double chin [4]. Results are not given in the registrations.
